title: GOOGL: Long, small. 25% core EPS growth at 22x with the Anthropic/SpaceX stakes as a free option; target $371.53 (+8.4%)
call_reason: The published target ($371.53) is above the $342.75 close, P(gain) is 0.59 and sizing conviction is medium, so this is a small, staged long. It is not a special situation.
one_liner: Alphabet trades at about 21x forward core EPS while FY2027 consensus EPS grows about 25% with revisions running 8 up to 1 down, Cloud grows 82% on a $514B backlog, and roughly $13-15/sh of SpaceX/Anthropic stakes carry a November IPO option. The edge is modest (+8% to target against 36% implied vol), so we buy 2 shares in two tranches around the Q3 print and keep the stop at $256.52.

thesis.point: Earnings compound at a multiple that already prices in the capex debate.
thesis.evidence: FY2027 consensus core EPS is about $14.92 (+25%), with 8 upward and 1 downward revision in 30 days. NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the horizon, at about 22x, gives $356-372 before stakes. The ~$257B 2027 capex consensus is already in that multiple.

thesis.point: Cloud is now a second profit engine, not an option.
thesis.evidence: Q2 2026 Cloud revenue grew about 82% with a $514B backlog, and TPU system sales to third parties begin in 2027. Backlog conversion is what supports FY2027 numbers while Search decelerates.

thesis.point: The equity stakes and base rates add a right tail at little cost.
thesis.evidence: SpaceX is about $82B (551M shares at $148.68, $14.1B locked until Q3 2027) and Anthropic is carried at $124.3B on a $47.6B cost. A reported November IPO at about $2T would add roughly $5-11/sh after tax. Separately, 9 of 10 prior 15% drawdowns were higher a year later; the one exception required EPS to fall 19%.

variant_view: There is no strong variant view; this is a modest long. We sit between two consensuses. Our $371.53 target is well below the sell side (49 analysts, mean $425.45, median $425, range $310-515, Strong Buy), because we apply about 22x NTM core EPS and haircut for 2027 capex, negative FCF and the $84.75B equity program, which the Street's ~$425 largely looks through. We are slightly above the options market: its distribution centers on $358.96 with P(gain) 0.554 and a 15th percentile of $247.69, against our $371.53, P(gain) 0.593 and $256.52. Our small premium to the options market comes from the fact-checked EPS revision trend and the stake/IPO optionality. The difference is about 3.5% of price, which is not enough to call it a mispricing.

valuation.methods: Supervisor-reconciled research target (12m) of $367 (range across five agents $360-375). The main method is NTM core P/E: about 22x on NTM core EPS of about $16.2-16.9 at the Sept 2027 horizon gives $356-372. Added to that are about $13-15/sh of after-tax stake value (SpaceX corrected to about $82B; Anthropic at its $124.3B carrying value) plus about $4-5/sh of probability-weighted Anthropic IPO uplift. A rolled-forward SOTP (about $370) is the cross-check. DCF cross-checks at $313-340 reflect the ~$257B 2027 capex consensus and are weighted about 20%. The published target of $371.53 is the median of the blended options/forecaster distribution, weighted 67% market and 33% forecasters; the expected value is $391.56 (+14.2%).

catalysts.event: Joint proposed Final Judgment due in the DOJ ad-tech case (court-ordered 30-day deadline after Judge Brinkema's Sept 2 remedies ruling; no AdX divestiture)
catalysts.why_it_moves: It locks in behavioral-only remedies (Prebid interoperability, bid-data sharing, a 6-year monitor) and removes the breakup tail. Most of this is already priced after Sept 2.
catalysts.watch: Disputed provisions submitted separately, the scope of the worldwide AdX rival-access terms, and Google's notice of appeal.

catalysts.date: Oct-Dec 2026 (Google says 'much earlier' than year-end; October rumored)
catalysts.event: Gemini 4 release (replaces the delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro)
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first test of model leadership after DeepMind talent departures and the Meta Muse launch. A strong launch would ease the 'Search gets disintermediated' fear; a slip or weak benchmarks would feed it.
catalysts.watch: Release date versus the October chatter, head-to-head benchmarks against OpenAI/Anthropic/Meta models, and Gemini app MAU and AI Mode usage disclosed alongside it.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings. Consensus core EPS is about $3.02 and revenue about $127B. Alphabet IR has not yet announced the call date.
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the first print since Meta Muse and the $84.75B raise, and the first official color on 2027 capex. Q2 showed that a capex surprise alone can move the stock down on a beat.
catalysts.watch: Search & other growth against Q2's +17% (single digits would signal a thesis break), paid-click trends, Cloud growth and the $514B backlog, any early 2027 capex framing against the ~$257B consensus, FCF after Q2's -$5.9B, ATM usage beyond sell-to-cover, and the GAAP SpaceX mark-to-market loss (excluded from core EPS).

catalysts.event: Meta Q3 2026 earnings: first quantified read on Muse agent engagement
catalysts.why_it_moves: Muse was the trigger for GOOGL's 3% drop on Sept 23. Strong Muse usage or commerce-query data would reinforce the Search-disintermediation narrative, while weak adoption would ease it.
catalysts.watch: Muse DAU/MAU, agentic shopping or query volume, and Meta's 2027 capex guide (a read-across on AI capex tolerance).

catalysts.event: Anthropic IPO at a reported ~$2T valuation, raising up to ~$100B
catalysts.why_it_moves: The IPO would re-mark Alphabet's stake, now carried at $124.3B on a $47.6B cost, and disclose the ownership percentage (estimated at 10-15%). That is about +$5-11/sh after tax at $2T. A slip or a lower price would remove part of the right tail.
catalysts.watch: A public S-1 flip (it typically comes about 15 days before the roadshow), Alphabet's disclosed ownership, the pricing range against $2T, and first-day trading.

catalysts.date: Oct 9, Oct 24 and Dec 8, 2026 (remaining SPCX insider lock-up tranches; Dec 8 is the final 180-day release)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Alphabet's ~551M SPCX shares (about $82B) move with SPCX. A 20% SPCX drop costs roughly $1.3/sh pre-tax, so this is a stake-value nuisance, not a thesis driver.
catalysts.watch: SPCX price reaction around each tranche. Alphabet's $14.1B long-term restricted block stays locked until Q3 2027.

catalysts.date: Q4 2026 - Q1 2027 (oral argument not yet scheduled; Google's reply brief due Sept 29)
catalysts.event: DC Circuit oral argument in the search monopoly appeal (Google appeals liability and remedies; DOJ cross-appeals for a default-payment ban and Chrome divestiture)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The argument itself only moves sentiment through the panel's questions. The ruling, likely mid-2027 or later, sets whether the Apple default payments and Chrome are at risk.
catalysts.watch: The scheduling order, panel composition, and the panel's questions on the payment ban and Chrome.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 earnings with the formal 2027 capex guide
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the single biggest swing factor. The FactSet consensus is about $257B (Evercore $262B). A guide far above that, with FCF negative into 2028 and more equity issuance, is the main path to the $250 thesis break. A guide at or below consensus paired with visible Cloud returns would re-rate the stock.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex against $257B, depreciation guide, FCF trajectory, whether buybacks resume, and Cloud operating margin.

risks.risk: Agentic assistants (Meta Muse, ChatGPT) take commercial queries, and Search growth falls from +17% to single digits, causing an actual EPS downgrade rather than multiple noise.
risks.signpost: Search & other growth below ~10% in the Q3 or Q4 print, decelerating paid clicks, strong Muse engagement numbers from Meta on Oct 28, and FY2027 EPS revisions turning net negative.

risks.risk: The capex/FCF spiral: the 2027 guide lands well above ~$257B, depreciation compresses margins, FCF stays negative and the $40B ATM or more equity dilutes beyond sell-to-cover.
risks.signpost: Q3 commentary pre-guiding 2027 capex well above $257B, another negative-FCF quarter, and ATM issuance well above RSU tax-withholding levels in the 10-Q.

risks.risk: An AI-valuation reset removes the stake credit: the Anthropic IPO slips or prices well below $2T, and SPCX keeps falling.
risks.signpost: No public S-1 by early November, a price range well below $2T, or SPCX breaking below about $120 (from $148.68).

risks.risk: Model competitiveness slips (Gemini 4 delay, DeepMind talent losses), undermining both Search defense and Cloud/TPU demand.
risks.signpost: Gemini 4 slipping into 2027 or trailing rival models on launch benchmarks, and further senior DeepMind departures.

trade.position: 2 sh (~$686, 6.9% of the $10,000 book); supervisor cap 12%. Size was set by the joint portfolio solve (overlap with AVGO, META and SPY), not by the stop budget.
trade.entry: Two tranches per the supervisor: buy 1 share now near $342.75 and 1 share after the Q3 2026 report (expected Oct 27). The second tranche goes in only if FY2027 core EPS revisions stay positive and there is no capex pre-guide far above the ~$257B consensus. A close below $250 cancels it.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit at the $256.52 stop (15th percentile), and in any case on a close below the $250 thesis break, which is about 17x FY2027 EPS with no stake credit. Take profit at $465.33. Add up to the 12% cap if Q3 shows Search at 12% or higher with Cloud backlog growing, or if the Feb 2027 capex guide is at or below about $257B with a credible FCF path. Also exit if the capex guide comes in far above consensus with FCF guided negative through 2028.

what_changes_our_mind: Search & other growth prints in single digits in Q3 or Q4 2026 while FY2027 EPS revisions turn net negative (the 2022 pattern). That would be a thesis break, and we would exit.
A February 2027 capex guide well above ~$257B (for example $280B+) with FCF negative into 2028 and further equity issuance. We would cut the position.

Upside case: Anthropic prices at or above $2T in November, Alphabet discloses 14% or more ownership, and Q3 shows Cloud backlog above $514B with stable margins. We would add to the 12% cap and raise the research target (12m).
